body.translated_text: <s>Cittaviśuddhiprakaraṇa</s> (Treatise on the Purification of the Mind)

children.translated_text: [Without beginning or end, peaceful, free from existence and non-existence,
free from conceptualization, without support, without fixed abode, non-dual,
without example, indescribable, inconceivable, without illustration,
without foundation, without establishment, without modification, unconditioned,
the refuge of all, the <s>Buddha</s>, whose body is made of compassion,
who shows various means to beings of various inclinations —
having bowed to the great passion, to the Lord <s>Padmanarteśvara</s> (Lord of the Lotus Dance),
I shall here speak briefly, from the examination of my own mind.
According to the <s>Yogācāra</s> system, everything is well established;
all that is to be stated here — therefore one should practice accordingly.]

children.text: yena yena hi bandhyante jantavo raudrakarmaṇā /
children.translated_text: By whatever terrible deeds beings are bound,

children.text: sopāyena tu tenaiva mucyante bhavabandhanāt // Cvp_6 //
children.translated_text: by those very means, skillfully applied, they are freed from the bondage of existence.
[From the purity of a being alone, a pure fruit is born;]
this has been stated very clearly and at great length in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
The Sage proclaimed the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) and <s>pudgala</s> (persons), and that all is mind-only;
from that, everything has arisen — fully in accord with the <s>Āgamas</s> (scriptural tradition).
Urged on by those seized by the possession of the demon of grasping at entities,

children.text: āgame 'pi hi suvyakto vistaraḥ karuṇātmanā // Cvp_9 //
children.translated_text: the expansion [of this teaching] in the <s>Āgamas</s> too is indeed very clear, by the compassionate one.
Mental phenomena are preceded by mind, are chief in mind, and are swift as mind;

children.text: manasā hi prasannena bhāṣate vā karoti vā // Cvp_10 //
children.translated_text: for with a mind that is pure, one speaks or acts.

children.text: svapitā bhikṣuṇā vṛddhaḥ śīghraṃ gaccheti preritaḥ /
children.translated_text: An old man, urged by a sleeping monk saying 'Go quickly!',
when he dies from falling — [the monk] is connected with an <s>ānantarya</s> (immediately retributive) offense.
When an <s>Arhat's</s> lip was rubbed with fragrant ointment, pressing the auspicious [mark],

children.text: upasthāyakabhikṣuḥ sa mṛte tasminna doṣabhāk // Cvp_12 //
children.translated_text: the attendant monk, when [the Arhat] died thereby — he was not a partaker of fault.
One who kills not a blind person, but with the perception of 'blind' — did not incur the fault;

children.text: ityuktaṃ vinaye vyaktaṃ na doṣo 'duṣṭacetasām // Cvp_13 //
children.translated_text: thus it is clearly stated in the <s>Vinaya</s>: there is no fault for those of unpolluted mind.
There is no fault in digging up a <s>stūpa</s>, when it is done with the intention of renovating it;
rather, it becomes solely a mass of merit, due to the cause being akin to [building] a <s>stūpa</s>.
By offering a pair of sandals on the head of the Sage, with a pure intention,

children.text: apanīya tathā cāndho rājyaṃ phalamavāpnutaḥ // Cvp_15 //
children.translated_text: and by removing them likewise, the blind man obtained kingship as his fruit.
Therefore, the determination of sin and merit is rooted in intention;
thus it is stated in the <s>Āgamas</s> — there is no offense for those of pure mind.
With a nature united with one's own presiding deity through <s>yoga</s>, with effort directed to the welfare of the world,

children.text: bhuñjāno viṣayān yogī mucyate na ca lipyate // Cvp_17 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s>, while enjoying sense objects, is liberated and is not tainted.
Just as one who knows the nature of poison, after examining and eating poison,

children.text: kevalaṃ muhyate nāsau rogamuktaśca jāyate // Cvp_18 //
children.translated_text: is merely stupefied but not killed, and becomes freed from disease,
seeing the entire world as resembling an illusion, a mirage, a <s>gandharva</s> city, and a dream —

children.text: jagatsarvaṃ samālokya kiṃ kathaṃ kena bhujyate // Cvp_19 //
children.translated_text: what is enjoyed, how, and by whom?

children.text: bālā rajyanti rūpeṣu vairāgyaṃ yānti madhyamāḥ /
children.translated_text: The childish are attached to forms; the middling attain dispassion;
those of supreme understanding who know the true nature of form are liberated.
Having contemplated the entire <s>samaya</s> (commitment) and the ritual of deity worship,
seeing it as pure, one should eat without hesitation what is enjoined by <s>mantra</s>.
Purification, awakening, and kindling — through the yoga of the three syllables;
and with the tips of the thumb and ring finger, one should gratify the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.
What the childish consider to be real is indeed false for the <s>yogins</s>;

children.text: gacchannantamanenaiva na baddho na ca mucyate // Cvp_23 //
children.translated_text: proceeding to the end by this very [path], one is neither bound nor liberated.
Those who do not see reality think of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: na saṃsāraṃ na nirvāṇaṃ manyante 'tattvadarśinaḥ // Cvp_24 //
children.translated_text: those who see reality think of neither <s>saṃsāra</s> nor <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
Conceptualization is indeed the great crocodile that causes one to fall into the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
the great-souled ones, free from conceptualization, are liberated from the bondage of existence.
Ordinary beings are afflicted by the poison of doubt, just as by [real] poison;
having uprooted that very [doubt] from its root, one should act with a compassionate nature.
Just as a clear crystal is colored by the color of another [object placed beside it],
so too the jewel of the mind is colored by the stain of conceptualization.
The jewel of the mind is by nature free from the stains of conceptualization,
primordially pure, unborn, without intrinsic nature, and undefiled.
Whatever is condemned by the childish, that very thing should be done with effort,
through union with one's own presiding deity — for the purpose of making the mind pure.
Women, bewildered by the fire-poison of passion, are desired by <s>yogins</s> of pure mind;
indeed they bring the fruit of both desire and liberation.
Just as one who, meditating on the <s>Garuḍa</s> mounted upon himself, draws out and drinks poison,

children.text: karoti nirviṣaṃ sādhyaṃ na viṣeṇābhibhūyate // Cvp_31 //
children.translated_text: renders the affliction non-poisonous — he is not overpowered by the poison.
A wheel twelve <s>yojanas</s> in diameter, spinning on the head —
by generating <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), it is removed — so says the scripture.
Having generated <s>bodhicitta</s>, with a mind set on <s>sambodhi</s> (perfect awakening),
there is nothing that should not be done, with the intention of saving the world.
Primordially pure, unborn, without intrinsic nature, and undefiled —

children.text: jagadbhāvena sampaśyanna baddho na ca mucyate // Cvp_34 //
children.translated_text: seeing the world in this way, one is neither bound nor liberated.
The <s>yogin</s>, having duly contemplated the extent of the deity's qualities,
is attached with a mind of passion — and through the enjoyment of passion is liberated.

children.text: kiṃ kurmaḥ kutra vai labhyā vicitrā bhāvaśaktayaḥ /
children.translated_text: What shall we do? Where indeed are the wondrous powers of existence to be found?

children.text: viṣākrānto yathā kaścidviṣeṇaiva tu nirviṣaḥ // Cvp_36 //
children.translated_text: Just as one overcome by poison becomes free from poison by poison itself.
As water is removed from the ear by water, and a thorn by a thorn,
so too the wise remove desire by desire itself.

children.text: yathaiva rajako vastraṃ malenaiva tu nirmalam /
children.translated_text: Just as a washerman makes a garment clean with dirt itself,
so too the wise one makes the self pure with impurity itself.
Just as a mirror becomes clean when rubbed with powder,
so too, when employed by the wise, a fault becomes the destroyer of faults.

children.text: lohapiṇḍo jale kṣipto majjatyeva tu kevalam /
children.translated_text: A lump of iron thrown into water simply sinks;

children.text: pātrīkṛto sa evāndhaṃ tārayettarati svayam // Cvp_40 //
children.translated_text: but that same [iron], made into a vessel, carries the blind across and crosses over itself.
Likewise, the mind made into a vessel through the method of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) —
while enjoying desire, one is liberated, and liberates others as well.

children.text: durvijñaiḥ sevitaḥ kāmaḥ kāmo bhavati bandhanam /
children.translated_text: Desire, when indulged by those who lack wisdom, becomes a bondage of desire;

children.text: sa eva sevito vijñaiḥ kāmo mokṣaprasādhakaḥ // Cvp_42 //
children.translated_text: that very desire, when indulged by the wise, becomes the accomplisher of liberation.
It is well known in the entire world that milk destroys poison;

children.text: tadeva phaṇibhiḥ pītaṃ sutarāṃ viṣavardhanam // Cvp_43 //
children.translated_text: yet that very [milk], when drunk by serpents, increases poison all the more.

children.text: jale kṣīraṃ yathāviṣṭaṃ haṃso pibati paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the wise <s>haṃsa</s> (swan) drinks the milk that is mixed with water,

children.text: saviṣān viṣāyāṃstadvad bhuktvā muktaśca paṇḍitaḥ // Cvp_44 //
children.translated_text: so too the wise one, having consumed the poisonous sense objects, is liberated.
Just as poison, when consumed according to the proper method, becomes nectar,
poorly consumed ghee and other rich foods become poison for the childish.

children.text: idameva hi yaccittaṃ śodhitaṃ hetubhiḥ śubhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: This very mind, when purified by auspicious means,
shines forth as free from conceptualization, without support, and pure by nature.
Just as fire, though small, when prepared with oil, a wick, and such,
becomes a lamp — pure, unflickering, steady, and the destroyer of darkness.
Just as a tiny <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan) seed, endowed with favorable conditions,
produces branches, roots, and fruits — becoming the maker of a great tree.
Just as through the combination with turmeric powder, a different color is known to appear,
so too, through the union of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), the wise know the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality).

children.text: ghṛtaṃ ca madhusaṃyuktaṃ samāṃśaṃ viṣatāṃ vrajet /
children.translated_text: Ghee mixed with equal parts of honey becomes poisonous;
yet that very same thing, consumed according to the proper method, becomes the most excellent rejuvenating elixir.

children.text: rasaghṛṣṭaṃ yathā tāmraṃ nirdoṣaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Just as copper, when rubbed with mercury, becomes flawless gold,

children.text: jñānaśuddhyā tathā kleśāḥ samyak kalyāṇakārakāḥ // Cvp_51 //
children.translated_text: so too the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), through purification by knowledge, become perfectly auspicious.
For those who have mounted the <s>Hīnayāna</s> (Lesser Vehicle), there is the fear of death at every step,
and the mind set on victory in battle stands far away indeed.
But one who has mounted the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), armored in compassion and <s>dharma</s>,
with the bow and arrow of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and the string [of method], with the intention of saving the world,
of great courage and great skill in means, of firm understanding and unwearied,
having won the difficult battle, would ferry others across as well.
Even animals suffer, being devoted solely to their own welfare;
blessed and rare are those people who work for the welfare of the world.
Those greedy for their own ends endure the sufferings of cold, wind, and such;

children.text: jagadarthapravṛttāste na sahante kathaṃ nu te // Cvp_56 //
children.translated_text: how then would those engaged in the welfare of the world not endure them?
Even the sufferings of the hells are to be endured by the compassionate;
who would even consider the sufferings of cold, wind, and such?
One should not contrive harsh austerities, nor perform rituals through fasting;

children.text: snānaṃ śaucaṃ na caivātra grāmadharmaṃ vivarjayet // Cvp_58 //
children.translated_text: neither bathing nor purification is required here — one should avoid village customs.
Nails, teeth, bones, and marrow arise from the transformation of the father's semen;
flesh, blood, hair, and such are born from the mother's blood.
This body, thus born from impurity, filled with impurity —

children.text: kathaṃ saṃstādṛśaḥ kāyo gaṅgāsnānena śudhyati // Cvp_60 //
children.translated_text: how can such a body be purified by bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> (Ganges)? // Cvp_60 //
For an impure vessel, even if washed with water again and again, [does not become pure];
likewise, this body, filled with impurity, is not purified. // Cvp_61 //
Even if it swims in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a dog does not deserve purification;

children.text: taddadvarmadhiyāṃ puṃsāṃ tīrthasnānaṃ tu niṣphalam // Cvp_62 //
children.translated_text: similarly, bathing at sacred fords (<s>tīrtha</s>) is fruitless for men of defective understanding. // Cvp_62 //
If <s>dharma</s> were [attained] by bathing, the fishermen would have achieved their goal;

children.text: naktandivaṃ jalasthānāṃ matsyādīnāṃ tu kā kathā // Cvp_63 //
children.translated_text: what then of fish and others who dwell in water day and night? // Cvp_63 //
It is certain that the destruction of sin does not come about through bathing,
since an increase of attachment and other [afflictions] is seen among those who frequent sacred fords. // Cvp_64 //

children.text: rāgo dveṣaśca mohaśca īrṣyā tṛṣṇā ca sarvadā /
children.translated_text: Attachment (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>), envy and craving — always

children.text: pāpānāṃ mūlamākhyātaṃ naiṣāṃ snānena śodhanam // Cvp_65 //
children.translated_text: these are declared to be the root of sins; their purification is not through bathing. // Cvp_65 //
These arise in beings from the grasping of self and mine;
that [grasping] too is caused by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and that <s>avidyā</s> is held to be delusion. // Cvp_66 //
Just as the perception of silver in a shell ceases when the shell is seen,
so too, through the vision of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), that [delusion] subsides, uprooted. // Cvp_67 //
Just as the perception of a snake in a rope ceases when the rope is seen,

children.text: sarpabuddhiḥ punastatra naiva syādiha janmani // Cvp_68 //
children.translated_text: the perception of a snake there would never arise again in this birth. // Cvp_68 //
Likewise, the perception of a [real] being (<s>sattva</s>) here ceases through <s>vajra</s>-knowledge (<s>vajrajñāna</s>);

children.text: na bhāvaḥ sambhavettatra dagdhabīja ivāṅkuraḥ // Cvp_69 //
children.translated_text: existence could not arise there, like a sprout from a burnt seed. // Cvp_69 //
This body, conjoined with the purity of selflessness, is primordially pure;

children.text: tasya santāpane dharmaḥ kaṣṭaṃ bālairvikalpitaḥ // Cvp_70 //
children.translated_text: the <s>dharma</s> of tormenting it through austerity is a painful [practice] fabricated by the childish. // Cvp_70 //
The conception of <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) depends on the rising and setting of the moon,
and the distinction of day and night [depends] on the rising and setting of the sun. // Cvp_71 //
The conventional usage of east and so forth is also made in dependence on conceptual construction;
planets, <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), and <s>rāśis</s> (zodiac signs) are all conceptualized by the world. // Cvp_72 //
Likewise, the conception of seasons depends on cold, heat, and rain;
this experience of the fruits of one's own <s>karma</s> arises from auspicious and inauspicious planetary [configurations]. // Cvp_73 //
The wise man who has set about to cleanse the wish-fulfilling jewel of the mind,

children.text: pravṛttaḥ kṣālituṃ vidvān ko 'vidyāṃ vṛṃhayetpunaḥ // Cvp_74 //
children.translated_text: which is smeared with the mud of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — who would nourish <s>avidyā</s> again? // Cvp_74 //
Without regard for planets, <s>tithis</s>, <s>nakṣatras</s>, place, time, and so forth,
one should abide free from conceptual construction, without [seeking] omens, and without apprehension. // Cvp_75 //
Whatever comes along the path of the senses, that by its own nature,
one who is well-concentrated in <s>yoga</s> should declare to be entirely pervaded by the <s>Buddha</s>. // Cvp_76 //
The eye is <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vairocana</s>; the ear is <s>Vajrasūryaka</s>;

children.text: ghrāṇaṃ ca paramāśvastu padmanarteśvaro mukham // Cvp_77 //
children.translated_text: the nose is <s>Paramāśva</s>; and the mouth is <s>Padmanarteśvara</s>. // Cvp_77 //
The body is the glorious King <s>Heruka</s>; and the mind is <s>Vajrasattva</s>;

children.text: evaṃ samyak sadā yogī vicaretkaruṇātmakaḥ // Cvp_78 //
children.translated_text: thus, the <s>yogin</s> should always rightly conduct himself, his nature being compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). // Cvp_78 //
That accomplished one (<s>siddhāntin</s>), free from conceptual construction, firm in resolve, rich in wisdom,
engaged in activities at will, enjoying all, and performing all. // Cvp_79 //
Performing all desired actions, conducting himself as he pleases,

children.text: utthito vā niṣaṇo vā caṅkramanvā svapaṃstathā // Cvp_80 //
children.translated_text: whether standing, sitting, walking, or sleeping — // Cvp_80 //
even one who has not entered a <s>maṇḍala</s>, even one with all obscurations,
through the <s>yoga</s> of one's own deity (<s>svādhidaivatayoga</s>), even one of little merit attains <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment). // Cvp_81 //
Through this, the state of all <s>Śūras</s> (heroes), or indeed the state of all <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: janmanīhaiva tattvajñaḥ samprāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ // Cvp_82 //
children.translated_text: the knower of reality attains in this very birth — there is no doubt. // Cvp_82 //
Just as the world of <s>yogins</s> is not obstructed by the ordinary world,
so too <s>yogins</s> are surpassed by those higher and higher through distinction of wisdom. // Cvp_83 //
Through great wisdom (<s>mahāprajñā</s>), great skillful means (<s>mahopāya</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākṛpā</s>), and devotion (<s>adhimokṣa</s>),
the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) is taught as the domain of great beings (<s>mahāsattva</s>). // Cvp_84 //
That which is not attained through innumerable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), according to many views —

children.text: janmanyatraiva buddhatvaṃ prāpyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // Cvp_85 //
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> is attained in this very birth; there is no doubt about this. // Cvp_85 //
The greatness of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, enriched by merit and wisdom,

children.text: sarvajñatvaṃ padaṃ ramyaṃ sadyo janmani labhyate // Cvp_86 //
children.translated_text: the delightful state of omniscience — is obtained immediately in this birth. // Cvp_86 //
Deliberation on scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and hearing is not grasped in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>;
from the non-differentiation of intention (<s>āśaya</s>) and latent disposition (<s>anuśaya</s>), the non-differentiation of vehicles is revealed. // Cvp_87 //
This devotion (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) is of another kind; the conduct of awakening (<s>bodhicārikā</s>) is likewise different;
the purification of mind (<s>cittaviśuddhi</s>) is also different — and the fruit is declared to be of another order. // Cvp_88 //
Just as in a clean mirror nearby, the form of one with clear eyes
shines very distinctly, pure and clear by nature — // Cvp_89 //
so too for <s>yogins</s>, whose minds are purified and freed from the net of conceptual construction,
knowledge [shines] through the stainless mirror of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). // Cvp_90 //
Just as a fire blazes suddenly in a sun-stone (<s>sūryakāntamaṇi</s>)
when embraced by the sunlight — [such is] tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>) in accomplishing one's purpose. // Cvp_91 //
The mind, like a sun-stone, having cast off the net of conceptual construction,
when well-embraced by the sun of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), blazes likewise for <s>yogins</s>. // Cvp_92 //
Just as fire blazes from the friction of two pieces of wood,
pure in the beginning, middle, and end, illuminating all things —
so too, they know, is the knowledge of the <s>yogin</s> through the union of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means). // Cvp_93 //
Just as this single lamp, resting on another wick,
according to its purpose and according to its location, produces illumination above — // Cvp_94 //
so one of infinite forms through radiant manifestation, through the cultivation of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means),
should perform appropriate actions for beings of various dispositions. // Cvp_95 //
Just as a knower of the method extracts nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) from milk,
faultless, cool, pleasing to the heart, and destroying all disease — // Cvp_96 //
so, from the milk of <s>prajñā</s> through great skillful means (<s>mahopāya</s>), arisen through churning like the method,
is the purified <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), the destroyer of happiness and suffering. // Cvp_97 //
Just as a creeper that has grown up is endowed with fruit and flowers,
so is the awakening in a single instant, conjoined with the two accumulations. // Cvp_98 //
Subjugation, repulsion, immobilization, causing rain, attraction, and so forth —
the <s>yogin</s> who delights in liquor and meat, even while performing these, is not stained. // Cvp_99 //
Why is a mirror needed to see a bracelet on one's own hand?
Since in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, even now, the power of <s>mantras</s> is visible. // Cvp_100 //
The relationship of mother and daughter is not truly conceived here;
like a broken incense stick, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has proclaimed [the nature of] the world. // Cvp_101 //
Semen, consisting of the five elements, and blood (<s>śoṇita</s>) likewise —

children.text: tanmayaḥ khalu piṇḍo 'yaṃ ko vipraḥ kaśca vāntyajaḥ // Cvp_102 //
children.translated_text: this body is indeed made of those; who then is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and who an outcaste? // Cvp_102 //
The entire body, consisting of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks),

children.text: anityaṃ duḥkhaśūnyañca na jātirna ca jātimān // Cvp_103 //
children.translated_text: is impermanent, [characterized by] suffering and emptiness — there is no caste, nor one who has caste. // Cvp_103 //
Someone born from the womb of a fisherwoman, another of <s>caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) birth —
through austerity one is born a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; therefore birth is not the cause. // Cvp_104 //
One's sister, mother, mother-in-law, one's daughter, niece,

children.text: brāhmaṇīṃ kṣatriyāṃ vaiśyāṃ vidhijñānena śūdrikām] // Cvp_105 //
children.translated_text: a <s>brāhmaṇī</s>, a <s>kṣatriya</s> woman, a <s>vaiśya</s> woman, a <s>śūdra</s> woman — through the knowledge of the ritual method — // Cvp_105 //
even a woman who is missing a limb, lowly, despised, or of outcaste birth —
one should always worship a woman through the cultivation of <s>jñānavajra</s> (knowledge-<s>vajra</s>). // Cvp_106 //
Always with a smiling face, with eyes expanded by <s>mantras</s>,
having generated the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), through the contemplation of one's own deity (<s>svādhidaivata</s>) — // Cvp_107 //
one should see for a moment whatever is to be seen; one should hear whatever is to be heard;
and one should speak, diligently, words free from truth and falsehood. // Cvp_108 //
Through bathing, anointing, clothing, eating, drinking, and so forth,
through the <s>yoga</s> of one's own deity (<s>svādhidaivatayoga</s>), one should contemplate the method of worship. // Cvp_109 //
Song, instrumental music, and dance — the practitioner of vows should enjoy with skillful means,
without making attachment to any of these states. // Cvp_110 //
Not by tormenting the self through austerity, nor by abandoning one's own being —
from bliss, just as one meditates on bliss, this unexcelled <s>Buddha</s> [state arises]. // Cvp_111 //
Through the enjoyment of all desires, one delights, free from fear;

children.text: mā bhaiṣṭa nāsti vaḥ pāpaṃsamayo duratikramaḥ // Cvp_112 //
children.translated_text: do not fear! There is no sin for you — the <s>samaya</s> (sacred commitment) is difficult to transgress. // Cvp_112 //
Even wood and so forth, consecrated by <s>mantras</s>, attain divinity;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ jñānavān kāyaḥkaṣṭaṃ mohaviceṣṭitam // Cvp_113 //
children.translated_text: how much more so a body endowed with knowledge — alas, the conduct of delusion! // Cvp_113 //
Having abandoned the pride of ordinariness, being concentrated,
one should perform this practice through the method of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means). // Cvp_114 //
Just as a lotus born from mud is not stained by the faults of mud,
so too the <s>yogin</s> is not stained by the faults of conceptual construction and latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>). // Cvp_115 //
Conceptual construction, resembling a reflection, is not stained by the faults of views;
just as the moon [reflected] in water is never stained by the water. // Cvp_116 //
The jewel of the mind, smeared with the mud of beginningless latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>),
when washed with the water of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), shines forth. // Cvp_117 //
For the wise one whose mind is steady in the yoga of one's personal deity (<s>svādhidaivatayoga</s>),
freed from the clouds of wrong views, the sun of the mind shines forth. // Cvp 118 //
[In the chapter on the measure of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), through the ascertainment of the true nature of things,
the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is to be accepted, and the error of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is to be abandoned. // Cvp 119 //
When the pot of conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) is suddenly shattered by the hammer of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),]
the lamp of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), naturally pure and clear, shines forth. // Cvp 120 //
The well-known elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) — earth, fire, water, and wind —
are transformed by the wise through the power of <s>mantras</s>. // Cvp 121 //
Abandoning all other doctrines, one should practice the doctrine of <s>mantras</s>,
by whose power even the state of bliss is accomplished. // Cvp 122 //
The Three Jewels (<s>triratna</s>) must not be abandoned, nor <s>bodhicitta</s>, nor the <s>guru</s>;
no living being whatsoever is to be killed — one should also maintain the <s>samaya</s> vows. // Cvp 123 //
Honey, blood, camphor mixed with red sandalwood,
and the <s>vajra</s>-water of the sage — these five also one should consecrate. // Cvp 124 //
And with other divine <s>samaya</s> vows that elevate the mind,
one should gratify the <s>vajra</s> of the mind for the purpose of pacifying the agitation of the winds (<s>vāyu</s>). // Cvp 125 //
[No impurity is to be suspected in the play of non-conceptual yoga;
with a mind thus united, the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should perform everything.] // Cvp 126 //
Even by a mere fly-drop of poison, one is overpowered;
the slightest aversion or doubt is coupled with the suffering of death. // Cvp 127 //
The wise one should either fight well or retreat well;
an in-between state is futile and indeed leads to a fall. // Cvp 128 //
One should not transgress the <s>guru's</s> command, the <s>mudrā</s>, or even his shadow;

children.text: guṇāstasya paraṃ grāhyā doṣānaiva kadācana // Cvp_129 //
children.translated_text: his virtues alone are to be grasped, never his faults. // Cvp 129 //
The <s>ācārya</s> (master) is the supreme deity, to be worshipped with effort;
he is <s>Vajradhara</s> himself, the king, established in his very form. // Cvp 130 //
Just as a water-purifying gem, itself pure, cleanses turbid water,
so the gem of faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is said to purify the jewel of the mind. // Cvp 131 //
Who does not go astray if they have faith but are deprived of the eye of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom)?
Therefore one should cultivate <s>prajñā</s> consisting of learning (<s>āgama</s>) and realization (<s>adhigama</s>). // Cvp 132 //
One who is faithful, learned, wise, and naturally compassionate —
he finds the means of happiness for the destruction of the world's suffering. // Cvp 133 //
Having established purity of mind (<s>cittaviśuddhi</s>), whatever happiness has been earned by me,
having established purity of mind, may people be made happy by that. // Cvp 134 //

body.translated_text: // This is the work of the venerable <s>Āryadeva</s> //
